ambient: Music built on atmosphere and texture rather than rhythm or melody: slow, spacious sound meant to be heard in the background as much as listened to. It took shape in the 1970s.
ambient techno: Techno with ambient textures: a steady but understated beat at slower tempos, built for home listening, often melodic or emotive.
chillstep: A calm, melodic offshoot of dubstep with ambient and chillout colours: half-time beats, soft pads and emotional melodies.
disco: Dance music of the 1970s built on a steady four-on-the-floor beat, a prominent bassline, strings and brass, and groove-heavy vocals.
downtempo: Relaxed electronic music at a slow to moderate pace, with a laid-back beat and warm, atmospheric sound. It grew out of the chillout scene of the 1990s.
drum and bass: Fast electronic dance music from the 1990s: breakbeats at around 160 to 180 beats per minute over deep sub-bass lines.
goa trance: Goa trance is a psychedelic electronic music style built around hypnotic rhythms, rolling basslines, and bright, intricate melodies. It grew from the beach parties of Goa, India, where DJs and travelers blended European electronic music with influences from Indian instruments and spiritual imagery. Tracks often unfold gradually: a steady beat anchors layers of bubbling synths, swirling effects, and repeating motifs that shift and bloom over time. The sound can feel both energetic and meditative, inviting listeners to dance while drawing them into a vivid, dreamlike atmosphere. Many compositions feature long builds and detailed arrangements, rewarding close listening as much as movement. Though rooted in the 1990s, Goa trance continues to inspire artists and dancers around the world with its colorful, expansive sound.
house: Four-on-the-floor dance music at a steady tempo, with a pulsing kick, repeating grooves and a warm bassline. It emerged in the 1980s.
neurofunk: A dark, technical style of drum and bass with heavy, twisting basslines, tight sound design and a cold, mechanical edge.
outrun: A synthwave subgenre named after the 1986 arcade game Out Run, tied to the retro 1980s look.
progressive house: A melodic, gradual style of house that builds slowly with layered synths and long transitions, usually at a mid-tempo pace. It emerged in the 1990s.
progressive trance: Trance that evolves slowly: gradual builds, layered melodies and a smoother, less abrupt structure than classic trance.
psytrance: Psychedelic trance: fast, driving electronic music with a rolling bassline and layered, twisting synth sounds, built for long, trance-like dancing.
singer-songwriter: A performer writing and singing their own songs, usually with just a guitar or piano; lyrics matter more than production. Includes the Russian author song (bard) tradition.
spacesynth: A melodic, synth-led strain of Italo disco from the early 1980s, with a steady dance beat, euphoric arpeggios and vocoder, mostly instrumental.
synthwave: Electronic music inspired by 1980s film scores, arcade games and synth-pop, with analog-style synthesizers, drum machines and a nostalgic, cinematic mood.
techno: Repetitive, machine-driven electronic dance music built on a steady kick drum and layered rhythms. It emerged in the 1980s.
trance: Melodic electronic dance music with repeating, hypnotic phrases and long builds towards an emotional peak. It emerged in the 1990s.
